ev.q: CDC analyzed data from 50,370 high school students (grades 9–12) who participated in the national Youth Risk Behavior Surveys
Unadjusted prevalence of each risk behavior was calculated by sleep duration.
Overall, 86.1% of students reported infrequent bicycle helmet use
Pairwise t-tests were used to assess significant differences compared with 9 hours
were adjusted for sex, grade, and race/ethnicity
Each national YRBS uses an independent, three-stage cluster sample design to obtain a nationally representative sample

methods_quotes.q: Logistic regression analyses were used to calculate adjusted prevalence ratios (APRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs)
were adjusted for sex, grade, and race/ethnicity
All analyses accounted for the sampling weights and complex survey design.
pairwise t-tests and ANOVA (i.e., linear trend) were used to assess crude significant differences.
P-values of <0.05 were defined to be statistically significant.
